title: Extraction Protocol for Untargeted LC-MS/MS from Microbial Cultures
author: Mauricio Caraballo
materials: The following are the steps for SPE : Specific protocols can vary from providers, so follow recommendations from the providers of the purchased product: Phenomenex, Sigma-Aldrich or Waters. Briefly, the steps are:
Optional: recondition cartridges for another SPE.

steps.title: Prepare metadata table
steps.instruction: Create a metadata table using the ReDU2‑MS2 Sample Information Template; fill all applicable fields, add any extra columns (e.g., co‑culture vs monoculture), and include at minimum the NCBI Taxonomy identifier (e.g., 1313|Streptococcus pneumoniae).

steps.title: Collect culture supernatant
steps.instruction: For liquid cultures, collect the supernatant; for semi‑solid cultures on agar, use the 96‑deep‑well plate protocol or a 96‑well SPE plate as appropriate.

steps.title: Add methanol and sonicate
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL methanol to each 1 mL of supernatant and sonicate for 15 minutes (00:15:00).

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 865 × g, °C, for 15 minutes to pellet cells and retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and store
steps.instruction: Transfer the clarified supernatant to a new 96‑well plate; if extraction will not be performed immediately, store the plate at –80 °C. Store the cell pellets separately at –80 °C until their extraction.

steps.title: Prepare SPE plate
steps.instruction: Set up a 96‑well SPE plate (compatible with 100 mg SPE cartridges) before extraction; see SPE steps below.

steps.title: Perform solid‑phase extraction
steps.instruction: Process the supernatant through the SPE cartridge using the following sequence.

substeps.instruction: Condition the cartridge with 2 mL methanol.
Equilibrate with 2 mL water (the supernatant is aqueous).
Load 1 mL supernatant (suitable for a 100 mg SPE cartridge).

steps.title: Dry extracts under vacuum
steps.instruction: Dry the 1 mL methanol eluates under vacuum; dried extracts are suitable for shipping to the Dorrestein Lab.

steps.title: Process cell pellets (endometabolome)
steps.instruction: Separate cells from culture by centrifugation or filtration, then handle the resulting pellets as described in subsequent steps.

steps.title: Add internal standard (optional)
steps.instruction: Add a known internal standard to each pellet extract to monitor extraction efficiency (optional).

steps.title: Quench enzymatic activity
steps.instruction: Quench metabolites by freeze‑drying or any other drying method (e.g., vacuum‑drying); dried samples can be shipped at this stage.

steps.title: Freeze‑thaw lysis cycles
steps.instruction: Subject the pellet plate to three freeze‑thaw cycles, each lasting 10–15 minutes (00:10:00–00:15:00), to lyse cells.

steps.title: Include blanks, standards, and labeling
steps.instruction: Include blanks of the culture media extracted under identical conditions, add any shipping standards, and record a sample map using 96‑well polypropylene deep‑well plates (2000 µL capacity, e.g., catalog E951033600) with sample names/labels.

steps.title: Replicates and shipping
steps.instruction: Prepare at least 3–6 biological replicates per sample and run technical replicates; ship dry extracts (and standards if possible) to the analysis laboratory.
